name: Delhi Outer Ring Road
history: The Outer Ring Road is one of Delhi's two great ring roads. It sweeps in a wide arc from the Wazirabad Bridge in the north, around the west and south of the city, to Kalindi Kunj in the south-east, with the Yamuna river closing the circle. It was built in stages and was in place by the mid-1980s, when it really was on the outer edge of Delhi; the city has since grown far past it, so today it is a busy inner artery rather than a bypass. Along the way it links big neighbourhoods like Rohini, Janakpuri, Vasant Vihar and Nehru Place, and it passes IIT Delhi, JNU and the Nehru Place business hub. Over the years Delhi's PWD has added more than a dozen flyovers and underpasses so traffic can keep moving, including a long signal-free run on the north-western arc between Vikaspuri and Wazirabad.
facts: About 47.5 km around, with six lanes of traffic.
Both ends of the road arc touch the Yamuna — at Wazirabad in the north and Kalindi Kunj in the south-east.
Has more than a dozen major junctions, including Mukarba Chowk, Peeragarhi and Chirag Delhi.
Passes major landmarks such as IIT Delhi and the Nehru Place business hub.
It was built as Delhi's outer bypass; the city has since spread well beyond it.
The Vikaspuri–Wazirabad stretch was made signal-free with a chain of flyovers and underpasses.
The cable-stayed Signature Bridge carries traffic across the Yamuna at the Wazirabad end.
Delhi Metro lines run alongside or above parts of the road.
significance: The Outer Ring Road is the main way to get across Delhi without going through the middle of it, and almost every big road out of the capital — the Karnal, Rohtak, Gurugram and Mathura roads — meets it somewhere. For millions of Delhiites it is the daily route to work, and for buses and goods vehicles it is the spine that ties the city's western and southern districts together.

engineering.name: Signature Bridge (Wazirabad)
engineering.note: Delhi's cable-stayed landmark bridge over the Yamuna, with a tall angled tower, opened in 2018

engineering.name: Rao Tula Ram (RTR) flyover
engineering.note: carries the ring road over the Delhi–Gurugram highway near Munirka — one of the busiest flyovers in the country

engineering.name: Chirag Delhi flyover
engineering.note: a long flyover over one of south Delhi's most crowded crossings

engineering.name: Vikaspuri–Wazirabad signal-free corridor
engineering.note: a chain of flyovers and underpasses on the north-western arc so traffic does not have to stop at lights

travelNotes: Traffic is heaviest on weekday mornings and evenings, especially around Rao Tula Ram, Chirag Delhi, Nehru Place and Mukarba Chowk. A full loop takes well over an hour in rush hour but under an hour late at night. Winter fog in December and January cuts visibility badly on the northern arc, and the underpasses on the western stretch can flood during heavy monsoon rain.
